findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed facility to have no sanitizer bucket set up during inspection. (CORRECTED) Discussed with PIC, and PIC mixed a sanitizer bucket at 400PPM of quaternary ammonium sanitizer. Ensure that kitchen staff have access to a prepared sanitizer bucket whenever food preparation is taking place.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
An employee was observed using bare hands to turn off faucet handles after the handwashing process. Discussed with PIC proper handwashing techniques. Ensure that employees use barriers to turn off faucet handles after the handwashing process to avoid recontaminating hands.  

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
There wasn’t any paper towels at the hand-sink in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC and paper-towels were provided to the dispenser. Be sure that paper towels are available at every handsink to ensure that hands are getting washed properly.   

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed a container of uncovered ice to be stored on a table in the serving area. The ice container is used for residents to serve themselves.  PIC noted that the facility will be getting a table top ice dispenser in the near future. Ensure that the container of ice is covered or served by employees to protect against contamination.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the can opener to be accumulated with food debris. Discussed with PIC and can opener was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that can openers are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent contaminating food. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Employee reporting agreements were not located during inspection.  Discussed with PIC and provided additional copies to be signed by employees.  Ensure every new kitchen employee signs agreement and reports are kept on-site for future inspections.

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Coffee machine was observed to contain an accumulation of debris above the coffee grounds basket.  Non food-contact surfaces shall be kept free of debris accumulation.  Ensure the coffee machine and water dispensing spout is cleaned regularly to prevent contamination.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas in need to be sealed or re-caulked:
-Holes in walls and NUDO board throughout the kitchen, especially around the dish machine
-Along the stainless steel above the single sink
-Along the stainless steel above the 3 part sink
-Along the mop sink
Inspector discussed with PIC who spoke to maintenance during inspection.  Ensure these areas are sealed or caulked to prevent mold growth and debris accumulation.

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Kitchen ceiling vents were observed to contain mold.  Discussed with PIC and maintenance during inspection.  Ensure vents are cleaned regularly to prevent mold accumulation.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Recently used mops were observed to be stored on the floor with the mop head down.  Discussed with PIC, mops shall be stored in a position to allow for air drying of the mop head.  COS

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed two half gallons of buttermilk with what appears to be mold in both of them. The two half gallons of buttermilk was discarded during the inspection.
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed a pan of uncovered peach cups in the walk-in cooler. Protect food at all times. Plastic was put on top of the peach cups during the inspection.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed an employee jacket and sweater stored in the dry storage room on the shelf with cans. Employee personnel should be placed in a designated area. The employee jacket and purse was removed during the inspection. Manager stated there is a employee locker room for staff belongings.
750-530c . Areas shall not be designated for that purpose if the use of  might result in the contamination of food, equipment, utensils or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed a melted, cracked spatula stored in the utensil drawer. The spatula was removed from the drawer and designated to scrap trays.
750-650b Equipment shall be designed to prevent cross-contamination of food or food contact surfaces by lubricants that it may require. Only food safe lubricants shall be used on equipment on or within food-contact surfaces.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
REPEAT: Observed a leak from the faucet at the three compartment sink. Repair the plumbing from the faucet at the three compartment sink.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floors in the dry storage room to have debris. Clean the floors in the dry storage room.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed boxes of catfish in walk in cooler stored above boxes of lettuce. Boxes of catfish were moved to bottom shelf to correct violation.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
REPEAT X1 - Observed spray sink table to not be caulked to the wall. Caulk this table-wall joint to make area smooth and easily cleanable,
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment: Observed two cans in the dry storage room to have multiple dents along the bottom seam of the can. Checking for sound condition of canned goods was discussed with dietician. Dented cans were segregated from the rest of the food in the establishment to be return for credit. The violation is corrected.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the spray sink table pulling away from the wall. Reattach table to the wall and caulk the joint to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the top of the dish machine to be soiled with some accumulation of food debris and lime scale deposits. Clean this non-food contact surface.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Facility currently has no Illinois Food Service Sanitation Manager Certificate for any current employees. A handout was provided for approved courses to obtain a FSSMC and upcoming classes at SCDPH. Provide at least one Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager during all hours of prep or service. A 90-day follow up inspection will be conducted.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a covered pan of bread sticks and corn bread to be molding and had a couple fruit flies trapped within the container. Item was discarded to correct the violation.
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
REPEATS 1x - 1) Observed the blade guard of the deli slicer to have an accumulation of dried food debris. R-2) Observed the blade of the can opener to be soiled with an accumulation of dried food debris. Wash rinse and sanitize these food contact surfaces after each use or at least once every four hours between uses.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the grease drain of the drip tray on the grill to be soiled with an accumulation of grease and food debris. 2) Observed the top of the dish machine to be soiled with an accumulation of food debris and lime scale. Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment:
Observed multiple containers in refrigeration being re-used to hold and store food not originally intended for different food items. Do not re-use single service containers. Provide proper containers for storage of food.
750-600 Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the following floors to be soiled: 1) floor under the fryer and grill are soiled with grease and food debris. CORRECTED> 2) Observed a soiled piece of card board next to the fryer on the floor. Cook noted the cardboard is used to catch grease from splashing on the floor. Cardboard was removed and replaced with a new, clean piece of card board. If facility is to use card board, replace card board daily. 3) floor below the steam well is soiled with food debris. 750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
REPEATS 1x- 1) Observed the wall damaged where paint and drywall surface has peeled to the left of the mop sink. R-2) Observed multiple small holes in the wall around the mop sink. R-3) observed the vent guard above the single door exiting the kitchen to be soiled with an accumulation of dust. NEW>4) Observed the wall to table joint behind the spray sink table to be soiled with what appears to be mold. 
NEW>5) Observed the wall above the hand sink upon entering the kitchen through the double doors to have paint peeled away. Repaint wall to make smooth and easily cleanable. 750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed two cans to be dented along seams. Make sure cans are not dented along seams upon receiving. Discard or return any cans that have dents along the seams.
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
A plastic container of rice was found on the prep table at 111degrees F (probe), at 2:35pm.  The cook who took the rice from the steam table had left for the day, and the time/temp of preparation was not labeled on the rice.  A second cook estimated the rice was removed from heat at 1:30.  CORRECTED - proper rapid cooling was discussed, and rice was immediately placed into an ice bath.  At ~3:10pm, manager decided to discard rice altogether.  Proper cooling was discussed, and handout and cooling labels given.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> 1) Observed milk with USE BY date of 11/27/2013. Manager could not let inspector know when milk was opened, so item was discarded. 2) Observed maple syrup held at room temperature in dry storage area. Syrup was labeled 11/20/2013 and stated on product label 'Refrigerate after opening'. Item was discarded
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
(A) Scoop inside sugar bin was found having fallen down into sugar.  CORRECTED - scoop was corrected so it is stored with handle upright.
(B) Knives were found stored in bucket of water in prep sink.  Manager states normally the stream of water from prep sink is continuous, creating their own potable dipping well.  However, in this position, the bucket of knives is exposed to food debris/splash from prep table.  Water was turned on and allowed to run into bucket to create their dipping well.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1) Observed cabinet in disrepair below coffee machine. Wood appears to have water damage and could be possible breeding area of fruit flies. Repair or replace cabinets at coffee station.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment:
Observed multiple food storage equipment to still have old date marking stickers and adhesive still attached to equipment. Pre-soak and scrape equipment to remove stickers and adhesive.
750-820c Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed under side of drink dispenser soiled with drink splash. Clean dispenser.
2) Observed moldy ice machine spout. Clean spout. 
3) Both sides of deli slicer blade are soiled w/ food debris (REPEAT).  Wash, rinse, sanitize and maintain all surfaces on deli slicer blade.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed mold in drain next to coffee machine from unused water dispenser. Clean drain. 
2) Spray sink table has mold along caulking where table meets wall.  Clean table and wall where mold is present.
3) Observed mold in collar of drain in lower cabinet below coffee machine. This area was observed to be an area where drain flies are present.
4) Unused Continental cooler next to dish machine/hand sink is soiled inside.  Clean this cooler.
5) Outside surfaces of both flour and sugar bulk containers are soiled with food splash.
6) Top of wall-mounted knife storage is soiled.
7) All non-food contact surfaces of table-mounted can opener should be cleaned (food splash).
8) Inside the left stove door has extreme grease and char accumulation around door frame and within stove.
Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
1) Observed a leak under the dish machine. Repair leak.
2) Observed leak on faucet of prep sink. Also, faucet is very loose.  Repair faucet.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed 10+ fruit flies and multiple drain flies in cabinet below coffee/drink station in dining area. It is possible that the damaged wood in the cabinet is a breeding site for flies. Also, the drain in the cabinet was soiled with mold and had drain flies coming out of pipe. Both the drain and the wood in disrepair need to be treated for fruit and drain flies. Cabinet should be repaired or replaced.
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the following floors to be soiled: 1) soiled floor in walk in freezer below shelves. 2) Floor soiled under dish machine (REPEAT). 3) Drain under steam table is soiled. 4) Drain under 3-pan sink is soiled (REPEAT).
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
(A) Observed the vent cover above door marked 'Do Not Use' to be soiled with heavy accumulation of dust. Clean vent cover.
(B) Air duct vent above walk-in cooler appears to  be moldy.  Clean this vent.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
A box of pepperoni, a box of ravioli, and a pan of beef stew in the walk-in freezer had condensation from the refrigeration unit that was frozen on the food.  The food was discarded to CORRECT the violation since the condensation could have contaminated it.

750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
A pan of jello salad in the walk-in cooler was dated "Use by 8-22-13."  The food was discarded to CORRECT the violation since it was past its 7day maximum holding time.

750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Raw bacon was stored above cookie dough and ice cream in the walk-in freezer.  The bacon was stored on a bottom shelf to CORRECT the violation.

750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
A bowl was used as a scoop in the white bulk corn meal bucket.   Replace the bowl with a scoop that has a handle and store the scoop in the food with the handle up or on a clean dry surface.

750-280 To avoid unnecessary manual contact with food, suitable dispensing utensils shall be used by employees or provided to consumers who serve themselves..

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
A test kit for checking the strength of the quat sanitizer was not available to the staff.  It may have been locked in the office.  Obtain a test kit and keep it available to the staff to use to check the strength of the sanitizer.

750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
1.  can opener blade and the black rubber mount the opener fits in.
2.  back side of the food slicer blade guard - food on it
3.  inside the door of the ice machine - small amount of black mold
Clean and sanitize these surfaces.

750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
1.  top of dish machine - lime build-up
2.  inside the left stove door - grease around the door frame and burnt food inside  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
3.  side of fryer and stove where they are side-by-side.
Clean these surfaces.

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
1.  Plates, saucers, and bowls were stored food side up / uncovered on a table to the left of the steam table. (REPEAT VIOLATION)  Invert of cover the utensils.
2.  Silverware was stored food end up in a storage unit in the food prep area. (REPEAT VIOLATION)  Store the silverware with the handles up to minimize hand contact with the eating ends.

750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
1.  The right faucet on the 3-pan sink was missing its hot and cold handles.  The faucet was leaking at the time of the last inspection.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)    Repair the faucet.
2.  The drain inside the cabinet under the coffee maker in the dining room is moldy and leaked water had damaged the wood around it.  Clean the drain and repair the cabinet bottom around it.
3.  The drain to the refrigeration unit in the walk-in freezer may be plugged up since ice is forming on surfaces above and below it.  Repair the drain on the unit if that is what is causing the ice formation.

750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment:
The dumpster lids were open.  Keep the lids closed.

750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
The following floors and drains were soiled.
1.  drain under the 3-pan sink (REPEAT VIOLATION) 
2.  drain under the dish machine 
3.  floor under the table with the mixer and toaster
Clean the drains and floor.

750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1.  The wall under the 3-pan sink was soiled.  Clean the wall.
2.  The sink to wall joint was moldy behind the spray hose to the right of the dish machine.  (REPEAT VIOLATION) Clean the gap and re-seal it.

750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
A light bulb was burnt out in the vent hood over the grill and stove.  Replace the bulb.

750-1230(a) Permanently fixed artificial light sources shall be installed to provide at least 20 foot-candles of light on all food preparation surfaces and at equipment or utensil washing areas.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
A certified Food Service Sanitation Manage (FSSM) was not on duty.   Have one or more employees become certified as a FSSM.  (NOTE:  Kitchen Manager Cheryl Martin had taken the day off.  Another employee had passed his FSSM exam and paid the state the $35 dollar fee for his license; however due to an error in filling out the form for the license, the state has not issued his license yet, per a phone call to the Illinois Department of Public Health during the inspection.  This employee was not present during the 1st hour of the inspection when some food was being prepared.)

750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Managers.
